summary: Kathleen Kenealy, research engineer at Google DeepMind and technical lead of the Gemma team, unveils the latest advancements in the Gemma model family at the AI Engineer World's Fair. She begins by contextualizing Google's long history of open-source AI contributions, including the Transformer, SentencePiece, and BERT, as well as infrastructure work on TPUs and ML frameworks (TensorFlow to JAX). Gemma is positioned as Google DeepMind's family of open-source, lightweight, state-of-the-art models built from the same research and technology as Gemini. Key advantages include responsibility by design (manual data inspection, safety evaluations from earliest experiments, rigorous final evaluations matching Gemini standards), unparalleled performance for model scale, high extensibility across hardware and frameworks, and open access with open licensing. The Gemma family has expanded since the February launch: Gemma 1.0 (foundational LLMs), CodeGemma (code generation/evaluation fine-tunes), Recurrent Gemma (state space model for efficient long-context inference, now in 2B and 9B sizes), Gemma 1.1 (improved instruction following and chat), and PaliGemma (multimodal model combining SigLIP vision encoder with Gemma 1.0 text decoder for image-text tasks, at 2B size). Kenealy announces Gemma 2 launch day, with 9B and 27B parameter models that outperform models 2-3x larger, with the 27B model competitive with Llama 3 70B and currently ranked #1 open model of its size on LMSYS. Gemma 2 maintains framework compatibility with Gemma 1, supports easy migration, has improved documentation and fine-tuning capabilities, and the 27B model is available in Google AI Studios. The Gemma cookbook on GitHub offers 20 recipes and accepts pull requests. GCP credits are available for research projects. Kenealy closes by sharing her personal motivation: having worked on Gemma for almost two years, she started the project because as an academic researcher she was disappointed by how far behind open foundational LLMs were compared to proprietary models. She encourages the audience to engage via Discord, GitHub, Hugging Face, and social media, and to share feedback on the models.

sections.title: Introduction and Google's Open Source AI History
sections.summary: Kathleen Kenealy introduces herself as research engineer at Google DeepMind and technical lead of the Gemma team. She contextualizes Gemma within Google's decade of open AI research (Transformer, SentencePiece, BERT) and infrastructure support (TPUs, TensorFlow, JAX).

sections.title: Gemma Key Advantages
sections.summary: Kenealy outlines Gemma's core advantages: responsibility by design (manual data inspection, safety evaluations from early development, rigorous final evaluations matching Gemini), unparalleled performance for scale, high extensibility across hardware and frameworks, and open access with open licensing.

sections.title: Gemma Model Family Variants
sections.summary: Overview of the Gemma model family expansion since February launch: Gemma 1.0 (foundational LLMs), CodeGemma (code generation/evaluation), Recurrent Gemma (state space model for efficient inference, now in 2B and 9B), Gemma 1.1 (improved instruction following), and PaliGemma (multimodal, SigLIP + Gemma 1.0, 2B size, for image-text tasks).

sections.title: Gemma 2 Launch Announcement
sections.summary: Announcement of Gemma 2 launch day with 9B and 27B parameter models. Gemma 2 outperforms models 2-3x larger, maintains framework compatibility with Gemma 1 for easy migration, has improved documentation and fine-tuning support. The 27B model is available in Google AI Studios.

sections.title: Gemma 2 Performance and Getting Started
sections.summary: Gemma 2 27B is competitive with Llama 3 70B, outperforms Grok models, and is ranked #1 open model of its size on LMSYS. Only the GPT-Large model outperforms it among open models. The Gemma cookbook on GitHub has 20 recipes and accepts pull requests. GCP credits available for research. Improved documentation and tutorials across frameworks.

sections.title: Closing Remarks and Personal Motivation
sections.summary: Kenealy closes by encouraging engagement via Discord, GitHub, Hugging Face, and social media. She shares her personal motivation: as a former academic researcher, she was disappointed by how far behind open foundational LLMs were compared to proprietary models, and has worked on Gemma for almost two years to close that gap. She invites feedback on the models.
